text:
elaine: heads-up — noticed gradual RSS increase on a handful of long streaming sessions (tool-loop + chat) over the last 48h. process stays healthy but memory never drops even after stream end.

hikaru: roughly how many tokens/kv entries per session? any common model or kernel config?

elaine: ~1.2M tokens in the worst repro we saw, kv resident pages ~450k by end. model is rdx/long-16k quantized, kernel-choice path using the new small-seq kernels from last rollout.

sam: fwiw we saw a similar slope last month but it plateaued. this one's growth is linear with time (not stepy). attached quick pprof snapshot:

sam: ```
# go tool pprof -top http://127.0.0.1:6060/debug/pprof/allocs
25.1%  runtime.mallocgc
13.7%  github.com/redwood/inference/kv.(*Page).retain
11.2%  github.com/redwood/inference/kv.(*Cache).EvictCandidate
 8.6%  github.com/redwood/inference/stream.(*ToolLoop).appendOutput
```

jordan: interesting that Page.retain shows up — suggests refs not released on eviction path. can you paste the evict log lines?

elaine: logs (filtered):

elaine: ```
EVICT start scan=0..450k want_free=10000
page=12345 state=stale refcnt=1 pinned=false
page=12345 evict_attempt ok=true reclaim=0
page=12345 final_refcnt=2 // <-- increased after evict_attempt
page=12346 state=active refcnt=3
...
```

hikaru: final_refcnt bump after evict_attempt is suspicious. maybe an iterator or toolloop goroutine re-acquired a view while eviction in flight.

sam: also correlates with the kernel-change commit abc123 (batching/kernels). that change added a small fast-path which holds a transient view for batching; if that path races with eviction we could leak a ref.

ops-bot: canary-deploy: rolling update rdx/long-16k -> kernel v2.1 applied to cluster-7 at 3432095000

elainE: (typo) meant to say elaine — ops-bot shows canary time lines up with regression start.

jordan: reproduction steps I used: run long-chat-driver with --tool-loop, seq_length=8192, concurrent_streams=2, and stress for ~6h. after run, run kv-stats:

jordan: ```
$ ./bin/kv-stats --addr localhost:9001
total_pages: 460123
resident_refs: 472230
pager_miss_rate: 0.003
stale_pages: 18k
page_chain_max: 120
```

hikaru: two hypotheses: 1) eviction increments ref incorrectly when handing page to fast-path batch, 2) reuse pool not returning pages to slab due to fragmentation/age-bucket mis-match. both could show same symptom.

sam: I instrumented the fast-path to log view acquire/release. small sample:

sam: ```
acquire view page=12345 batch_id=891
release view page=12345 batch_id=891
# but sometimes release missing for 12345
```

elaine: i pushed a local hack that forces eviction to spin-wait and check for outstanding views before deciding reclaim; that reduced leak slope in my runs (6h -> RSS flatter). not a fix but a clue.

jordan: can we add a small e2e test around batch fast-path + eviction? something that repeatedly creates transient batch views and triggers evict scan. i can sketch one.

hikaru: agreed. also add a jemalloc/prof snapshot right before/after eviction sweep to see if slab fragmentation correlates. i suspect the age-bucket rotation in kv-compact changed in abc123 and left orphaned page anchors.

sam: proposed quick patch: decrement view ref in evict path if page was handed out to batch but not yet in use (race window). PR draft title: fix(kv): clear transient batch ref on evict.

elaine: please mark as urgent for canary. if we don't fix, long-running tool-loop customers will see creeping memory and sysadmins will restart processes.

ops-bot: jira RED-1482 created by hikaru: "kv: transient batch-view ref leak causing longstream RSS growth"

jordan: next steps: 1) add e2e repro test 2) land small fix 3) run 48h canary with extra kv-metrics (resident_refs, stale_pages, page_chain_max) 4) roll if stable.

sam: perf note: watch for perf regressions from extra atomic ops in evict path. maybe make it conditional under assert or telemetry mode if needed.

elaine: thanks — i'll coordinate the canary and post results here. if anyone finds a simpler repro or a blunter mitigation (periodic full-compact that forces page reclamation) post it. :thumbsup:

hikaru: i'll take the PR review.

sam: +1

elaine: updating thread when i have canary graphs (RSS, resident_refs).
